source_snapshot.title: UAE taxi drivers cannot refuse you or overcharge from January 2027: What the new traffic rules say
source_snapshot.text: Dubai: Have you ever waited for a while to flag down a taxi, only to be told by the taxi driver that he will not take you to your destination? Under the new provisions to UAE’s traffic regulations, this kind of behaviour is prohibited. When it comes to hailing taxis, here’s what you need to know, so that you’re better informed of your rights as you commute around Dubai. What are the new regulations around hailing taxis? The new implementing regulations governing the UAE's Federal Traffic Law provide a comprehensive framework. Cabinet Decision No. (174) of 2026, concerning the Implementing Regulations of Federal Decree-Law No. (14) of 2024 on the Regulation of Traffic, introduces a range of new provisions scheduled to take effect on January 1, 2027. Among the key changes are regulatory frameworks for electric scooter and bicycle permits, additional road safety requirements, and rules addressing the obligations of taxi drivers. Can a taxi driver refuse a passenger? Article (36) of the UAE's Federal Traffic Law explicitly states that taxi drivers cannot refuse to transport a passenger who is willing to pay the determined fare, without reasonable justification. The law makes an exception in this situation for when the taxi has already reached its maximum passenger capacity. Can a taxi driver increase the fare? The new provisions also highlight that taxi drivers may charge only the amount prescribed by the competent entity in the emirate. They cannot demand a fare exceeding the prescribed amount. Can a taxi driver carry extra passengers? Placing a child on your lap or asking the taxi driver if it is okay to squeeze in just one more person, despite a full back seat, may seem like an innocuous request. But Article (44) of the law prohibits taxi drivers from allowing more passengers into their vehicles than the number authorised by the licensing authority. The standard limit for a sedan taxi is four passengers, with larger vans or multi-purpose vehicles carrying up to six passengers, with everyone required to buckle in their seat belts. To confirm passenger limits, refer to the taxi’s identification details. Article (44) requires taxi drivers to prominently display a plate that highlights the vehicle's licence plate number in Arabic and English, along with the authorised number of passengers permitted in the vehicle, and any other particulars prescribed by the licensing authority. The plate can typically be found on the back of the front passenger seat, or displayed above the glove box. What are other rules that taxi drivers must follow? Article (36) of the UAE's Federal Traffic Law lays out the following obligations for taxi drivers to follow. They must: Stop to allow passengers to board or alight only at places designated for that purpose. Park and remain stationed for extended periods only at taxi stands, the locations and permitted vehicle capacities of which, are announced and indicated by signs and road markings. Refrain from refusing to transport any person willing to pay the fare prescribed by the competent entity in the emirate, without justification, unless the vehicle has reached its permitted passenger capacity. No fare exceeding the prescribed fare may be demanded. Refrain from being distracted by conversations with others. Comply with additional instructions issued by the relevant licensing authority or traffic police.

source_verification.reason: All factual claims in the post are directly supported by the source text.

claims.claim: From January 1, 2027, taxi drivers in the UAE cannot refuse passengers without a valid reason.
Taxi drivers cannot charge more than the established fare.
The maximum number of passengers in a taxi is limited by the license: usually four for sedans and six for larger vehicles.
Taxi drivers must stop only at designated places.
Taxi drivers must comply with traffic rules.
Information about the maximum number of passengers and license number must be visible inside the taxi.

title: UAE taxi drivers cannot refuse you or overcharge from January 2027: What the new traffic rules say
summary_ru: 🚇 Новые правила для таксистов в ОАЭ с января 2027 года 📅 С 1 января 2027 года таксисты в ОАЭ не смогут отказывать пассажирам без уважительной причины и брать плату выше установленной. Максимальное число пассажиров в такси ограничено лицензией: обычно это четыре человека для седанов и шесть для больших автомобилей. Таксисты обязаны останавливаться только в специально отведённых местах и соблюдать правила дорожного движения. Информация о максимальном числе пассажиров и номере лицензии должна быть видна в салоне.
